title: edge-proxy-idempotency-safeguard-and-staged-telemetry-rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: During a customer escalation (enterprise tenant: AtlasFinance) we observed recurring bursts of 5xx and long tail timeouts across hosted inference. The pattern was triggered by an edge-level retry amplification combined with idempotency token loss between front-door edge and runtime adapters. The behavior manifested as repeated hedged requests being accepted by the backend runtime, which caused queue saturation, kvcache churn, and downstream 5xx timeouts for affected tenants.

Root cause hypothesis validated: 1) A recent edge proxy change (edge-proxy v2.3.1) modified connection reuse heuristics and rewrote the order of headers when proxying requests. 2) A concurrent connection-pool patch in dedicated-adapter reduced the strictness of idempotency header validation to maintain throughput under load. 3) When client SDKs retried (SDKs using default hedging in 3rd-party libs), the combination allowed requests with identical original idempotency tokens to arrive with mutated header order and occasionally missing tracer fields. The runtime deduplication logic was strict on header canonicalization; missing canonical headers bypassed dedupe and increased backend work. 4) Tenant-scoped admission thresholds were not applied at the edge layer for hedged requests, which allowed multiple duplicates through during tenant surges.

Why unique/important: Previous tickets focused on connection pool starvation and naive retry storms. This incident was subtle because the trigger was header reordering + weakened dedupe logic, not just brute force retry volume. That made the problem intermittent and customer-visible only during specific client SDK retry patterns and tenant activity spikes.

Goal: Ship a guarded fix that prevents idempotency loss from header reordering, adds an edge-level deduplication admission shim, and deploys with staged telemetry so we can observe interactions with dedicated adapters and legacy SDKs without risking global regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy preserves a canonical idempotency header (X-Redwood-Idempotency) and will forward a normalized header order to runtime adapters for all proxied calls.
Introduce an edge admission layer that deduplicates hedged requests by short-lived token cache (1s TTL) and rejects/fast-fails clear duplicates with 409 + structured telemetry for diagnostics.
Add tenant-aware jitter and cooldown to hedging behavior at the edge so surge-induced duplicates are exponentially reduced for noisy tenants.
Automated integration test reproduces the header-mutation pattern and validates dedupe path in CI.
Canary rollout plan executed: 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100% with telemetry dashboards showing per-tenant retry count, dedupe hits, P50/P95 latency, and backend queue depth.
Customer AtlasFinance confirms stability over a 48h observation window after canary completion.
Documentation updated: runbook and SDK guidance on idempotency and hedging best practices.
Postmortem published with remediation owners and preventive tasks scheduled.
updates: 2025-01-20: Initial triage by on-call. Alert pattern: repeated 5xx spikes for tenant 'atlas-finance' starting 2025-01-19 22:10 UTC. Pager duty tipped us via SEs. Added surge-mitigation label and assigned to Ravi.

2025-01-21: Captured traces and request headers for sample timeframe. Noticed X-Redwood-Idempotency sometimes absent or reordered when proxied through edge-proxy v2.3.1. Created synthetic replay harness to reproduce header mutation locally.

2025-01-22: Reproduced amplified backend load in staging by running hedged clients (SDK v1.12 default hedging) while toggling edge header canonicalization. Confirmed runtime dedupe bypass when header canonicalization differs.

2025-01-24: Implemented two-pronged fix: (A) edge-proxy change to canonicalize and persist X-Redwood-Idempotency header, (B) short-lived edge-level token cache to fast-fail duplicates before they hit runtime. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1298

2025-01-26: Hotfix PR for dedicated-adapter reintroduced stricter idempotency validation to align with edge canonicalization: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dedicated-adapter/pull/874. Coordination with infra to avoid version skew during rollout.

2025-01-28: Integration tests added to CI to simulate header reordering and hedged requests. Local benchmark of admission shim shows median additional edge latency of +0.8ms under normal load, acceptable per SLOs.

2025-01-30: Canary 1 (5% tenant population) started. Observed dedupe hits ~= 0.3% of requests for canary tenants and backend queue depth decrease by ~18% for those tenants. No customer escalations from canary group.

2025-02-02: Canary 2 (25%) expanded. AtlasFinance opted into canary early and reported reduced error rates. Noted an unexpected increase in 409 rejects for one legacy internal integration; rolled a compatibility shim to accept X-Idempotency-Alt header for older SDKs.
2025-02-04: Full rollout completed for edge-proxy canonicalization. Monitoring dashboards updated with retry/dedupe panels. Preparing PR for postmortem and runbook updates.

2025-02-05: This ticket moved to In Review. Requested security review waiver (no secrets changed). Awaiting reviews on edge-proxy and dedicated-adapter PRs and a signoff from Solutions Engineering to close.
mitigation_runbook: If a customer escalates with high 5xx: 1) Enable tenant fast-path quarantine from console (Emergency -> Quarantine tenant) to route to dedicated fallback model. 2) Increase edge-admission TTL to 2s temporarily to reduce duplicate acceptance. 3) If 409 surge observed, add compatibility header alias (X-Idempotency-Alt) and monitor dedupe-hit ratio. 4) Engage SE and Account team, provide temporary rate-limits and advise SDK upgrade. 5) Post-incident: run the synthetic hedging harness against canary to validate regressions.
postmortem_actions: Owner: Ravi Kapoor - finalize runbook and close compatibility gaps with older SDKs (due 2025-02-14)
Owner: Maya Chen - update public runbook and customer-facing KB for idempotency and retry guidance (due 2025-02-10)
Owner: Infra - add telemetry alert for idempotency-header-drop-rate (due 2025-02-12)
Owner: Platform QA - add synthetic hedging tests to nightly regression suite (due 2025-02-17)
Owner: Product - review SDK defaults for hedging and consider disabling hedging by default in next SDK minor release (due 2025-02-28)
